summary: AIDC-AI/ComfyUI-Copilot — An AI-powered custom node for ComfyUI designed to enhance workflow automation and provide intelligent assistance. Repo-surface review: measured from the public repository (5375 stars, MIT, last push 2026-04-07); not hands-on tested.

hlido_opinion.headline: A mature, MIT-licensed AI copilot for ComfyUI with real traction and a v2 release — but a ~100-day quiet stretch is the signal to watch.
hlido_opinion.body: By repository signals this is a credible, adoptable addition to a ComfyUI image pipeline: 5.4k stars, an MIT license, a reached v2.0 release, TypeScript with CI present, and a documented install. It targets a real and popular host (ComfyUI), which grounds its usefulness. The one caution the repo surface raises is momentum — the last push was roughly 100 days ago, just outside the 90-day active-development window, so confirm it still tracks the current ComfyUI before depending on it. Repo-surface read; the quality of the in-canvas assistance itself is not something we tested hands-on.

tier_rationale: STEADY (82, repo-surface ceiling). MIT licensing, a v2.0 release, CI, documented install and strong traction against a popular host clear STEADY. VITAL is withheld because repo signals cannot verify functional quality, and the ~100-day gap since the last push flags cooling momentum.
what_it_does_well: Reached a v2.0 release — a maturity signal
Targets a real, widely-used host (ComfyUI), grounding its utility
what_it_fails_at: ~100 days since last push — momentum cooling, just outside the active-development window
Agent-consumability is via a ComfyUI node, not a general agent interface
Functional quality unverified from the repo surface
best_for: ComfyUI users wanting in-canvas AI assistance
Image/design workflows already standardized on ComfyUI
not_recommended_for: Teams needing a guarantee of active maintenance
Agent pipelines needing a standalone programmatic API

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Runs as a ComfyUI custom node; consumable inside a ComfyUI-hosted workflow rather than as a standalone agent API. No hands-on behavioral test performed.
